title: Revised Code of Washington, Title 50A - Family and Medical Leave
verified_how: fetched https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=50A (HTTP 200): breadcrumb 'Home / State laws and rules / RCWs / Title 50A', heading 'Title 50A RCW - FAMILY AND MEDICAL LEAVE', chapter list 50A.05 (General provisions), 50A.10 (Premiums), 50A.15 (Benefits), 50A.20 (Employer requirements), 50A.24 (Small business assistance), 50A.25 (Privacy), 50A.30 (Voluntary plans), 50A.35 (Employment protections), 50A.40 (Unlawful acts), 50A.45 (Limitations, disqualifications, penalties, and interest) and 50A.50 (Appeals), with a 'Title digest PDF' link; no chapter marked repealed. Currency: the RCW index page (https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/) states 'Last update: July 15, 2026' and explains that 'The online version of the RCW is updated twice a year, once in the early fall following the legislative session, and again at the end of the year if a ballot measure that changes the law passed at the general election'; it also records that 'The Statute Law Committee declares that the certified PDF publication documents in the RCW Archive area on the Office of the Code Reviser's website constitute the official publication of the Revised Code of Washington', so this HTML version is the working rather than the certified text. The register flags amended-but-not-yet-merged text by printing a section two or three times with '(as amended by 2026 c NN)' suffixes.
notes: This is Washington's Paid Family and Medical Leave programme - a whole RCW title, which is why the title rather than a single chapter is listed. Washington's paid sick leave mandate is elsewhere, in the Minimum Wage Act (RCW 49.46.200-.210), and there is no Washington statute requiring paid public holidays or paid vacation for private-sector employees.
